findings.summary: The new affordance says either party to the block may remove it, but the operation and the Block invariant restrict removal to the blocker only.
findings.evidence: affordance effects: "Either party to the block may remove it" vs operation.block.remove preconditions: [Caller is the blocker] and Block invariants: "Only the blocker can remove it"

findings.summary: The affordance precondition makes Remove block available whenever any block exists between the two accounts, including to the blocked party, which conflicts with blocker-only authority.
findings.evidence: preconditions: [A block exists between the owner and this contact's linked account]; failure: [Not available when no block exists]
